note: Merged from batch files; interrupted batches were finished by further independent agents with the same instructions (part names record which).

scores.notes: Icon style: one wheeled throne made of flame sits centre inside a cloud-ringed fire oval, its seat empty of any face, hair or robe; Daniel, small at bottom centre in an indigo fringed cloak, looks up. Gold ground and the green ground band reach all borders with no lettering, but the city at upper left and right has domes topped with small crosses (an anachronism).

Watercolor painted to all four borders: Jesus centre with right arm extended toward the tomb, Lazarus in grave linens standing in the dark tomb mouth, stone rolled aside, Martha beside Jesus with hands at her chest, crowd on both sides. Jesus's head is level rather than lifted, a minor deviation.
Haloed elder on a stool points at a scroll unrolled on the ground (lower centre) whose lines are rendered as glyph-like script; youth by the doorway and lamp/jar on the ledge are as requested.

Peter stands on a wooden pier/plank floating in the open sea (lower left) holding a coiled net and steps toward the boat at right, rather than stepping down from the boat onto the water; Jesus stands on the water centre under the cloud break and disciples row in the boat. The pier in mid-sea and stepping direction contradict the moment.

Icon style: about twenty exiled men, women and children sit on the reed-lined bank across the foreground, heads bowed and hands at their faces, with Babylon's brick walls, a blue-tiled gate and a ziggurat beyond the river. Gold ground and figures reach all four borders, and the gate shows tiles but no inscription.

Soldiers casting lots over folded garments, with the crucified Jesus at a restrained distance upper right, but the watercolor leaves white unpainted paper along all four edges, deckled at top-left. The titulus on the cross (~x1075-1100, y30-50) carries INRI-like glyph squiggles.

Throne at centre is empty radiance under a rainbow with no figure; lion, calf, man and eagle creatures with eyed wings stand on a glass-block crystal sea. Pale watercolor washes thin near left/right edges but ink drawing runs off all borders.

Elder on a stool in a mudbrick courtyard points at an open scroll covered in rows of glyph-like script (centre), young listener in the doorway right, lamp and jar on the ledge. Scene matches, but the scroll lettering is visible text.

Icon style: Job sits upright on a grey ash heap with broken pottery in the lower centre, gripping a staff and looking up at a dust whirlwind with a fiery core at top centre; the core is only swirling flame and cloud, with no face or figure. A walled town is at left; gold ground and earth reach all borders, no lettering.

Dark oil interior painted to all borders: the Levite stands mid-ground with the knife held low, and the concubine lies intact and covered on a mat in the foreground. A clay lamp sits on the bench at left and the donkey shows in the grey doorway. The handling is restrained, with no gore.

Roles inverted: haloed Jesus stands inside the boat with the disciples (centre-right) while Peter, carrying nets and a pole, walks over the waves toward the boat (left), contradicting Peter stepping down from the boat to come to Jesus.

Fire streaks fall from dark clouds onto two walled cities among palms and fields, fleeing figures on the right, Zoar distant, sunrise; no face or figure in the clouds. The watercolour breaks to white unpainted paper along the left edge (upper sky and lower-left), the right edge, and the bottom-left corner.

Icon style: Ezekiel, with a faint halo, stands right of centre raising one arm beside a wide field of skulls and bones under a gold sky, with no divine figure anywhere. He oddly holds a blank clipboard-like writing tablet and stylus in his other hand; paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

Ezekiel stands upright with his arm raised over a valley of scattered skulls and bones stretching to the horizon under amber late-afternoon cloud. The sky has no face or figure, and the paint reaches all four edges.
Saul halts in the road with head lifted under a shaft of light from the sky (centre); no figure inside the light; companions shield their eyes at right and Damascus walls sit on the left horizon.

Icon-style Shulammite stands at left third in red mantle among roses and lilies, gesturing to the blossoms, with vineyards, stone houses and a shepherd's staff lying in the flowers at right; gold sky reaches all edges, faint halo line only, no lettering.

Icon style: the Levite stands centre with a knife held low and a staff, over the robed concubine lying on a mat in the foreground with open eyes; a donkey is in the doorway at right, and a clay lamp and folded cloak are on the bench at left. A faint incised halo circles the Levite's head (subtle but theologically odd); the interior reaches all edges, no lettering.

Icon-style elder on a stool pointing into the scroll on his knees, a boy listener by the doorway, and a lamp and jar on the ledge, all matching the plan. The open scroll (~x570-800, y430-630) shows about 13 lines of legible pseudo-Latin capital letters.

Job sits on the ash heap among potsherds gazing at a towering dust whirlwind with a fire-lit core (centre-top); no face, hands or human shape in the storm; loose washes but painting reaches all borders.

Jonah sits hunched with a dark cloak drawn around him inside a ribbed, glistening red-grey fish interior, feet in dark water, with faint golden glow through the walls; God appears only as that glow. Small gold-leaf spandrels show in the top-left and top-right corners outside the arched ribs, but they are painted ground, not paper or an ornamental border.

The unrolled scroll on the wall in the lower centre-right is covered in dense pseudo-Hebrew glyph lines, and the watercolour fades into unpainted cream paper along the lower-left edge and corner. The scene otherwise matches: an old man and a woman with a water jar at left, two Roman soldiers on the road, three men talking, and a child in a doorway at right.

Soldiers divide garments with the crucified Jesus on the cross upper right, but an unrequested Jesus look-alike stands among them (long centre-parted hair, beard, white robe with blue mantle, hands clasped; centre ~x795, y270-470), so Jesus appears twice. Further unrequested civilian onlookers stand at right.
Elder on a stool with scroll on his knees pointing at lines rendered as pseudo-Hebrew glyph script (lower centre); youth at the doorway and lamp/jugs on the ledge match the scene.

Peter steps from the boat's gunwale onto the waves toward Jesus, who stands on the water at right under a moonlit cloud break, disciples in the boat at left; Peter oddly carries a net and a pole. A painted signature scrawl is visible in the bottom-right corner (around 1230-1300 px across, near the bottom edge).

Oil painting: a barefoot child stands centre with an open hand among a wolf lying with two lambs, a leopard with a young goat, a young lion, two calves, a lioness and a small calf at left; four villagers watch from the path at right, with terraces, a village and a walled city with a temple on the distant hill at upper left. Paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

Oil scene matching the plan: an elderly man on a stool points along the scroll on his knees, a boy stands in the doorway, and a lamp and jar sit on the ledge. The scroll (~x500-810, y400-590) is filled with lines of Hebrew-like pseudo-script.
Death-bed scene matches (Adam on woven mat, kin kneeling, tents, well, goats), but the watercolor fades into white paper with splatter on all four edges, strongest at left and bottom.

David reclines on his elbow in lush grass beside a still pool with grazing sheep, a crook, a stone fold wall and olive trees; a sword and harp lie by him. He is large in the right foreground rather than small in a high wide view; pale watercolour sky at top-left still reaches the border.

Ink-and-watercolour: white-bearded Moses with a crook staff leads a long column of families with children over the seabed between tall green water walls, under a stormy night sky. The requested pillar of cloud and fire is absent, so there is no divine figure; the left wall takes a red tint from the cliffs behind it, a walled town sits on the far shore at upper right, and the wash reaches all edges with no lettering.

Icon-style Paul in a dark cloak on a hillside path, face lifted to a gold sky, with the coast and fishing boats below, travellers on the road, and two red-cloaked Roman soldiers lower right. Paul is large and central rather than small, which is minor; God is mentioned in the verse but not depicted.

Adam lies on a mat with folded hands surrounded by kneeling, praying kin; jar, tools, goats, tents and mud-brick town behind; edges fully painted (only a negligible dark compression block in the top-left corner).

Four kneeling Roman soldiers divide garments and dice in the foreground with the crucified Jesus on a cross centre-back against gold, titulus blank. Two onlookers stand at left (one with a halo, a saint/apostle) and two more at right (a figure in a blue mantle and an elder), people the soldiers-only scene does not include.

Oil painting: Jesus stands centre in the boat with arm extended, about ten disciples around him gripping the gunwales, torn sail and lantern on the mast, golden break in the storm clouds. Paint reaches all four borders; no lettering in any corner.

View from inside the pit: Daniel centre with face lifted, lions with closed mouths, Darius leaning over the rim. A fully formed translucent winged angel with face, hair, robe and outstretched hand stands right of Daniel (~x850-1000, y280-540), although the scene asked for only the radiance of an unseen angel; it is not God, but it may not be allowed.
Job sits upright on the ash heap with broken pottery, facing a dark whirlwind with fire-tinged light rising behind; no face or figure in the cloud or fire.

Jesus stands upright on the boat's raised deck, arm extended over the water, framed against breaking clouds with dawn light; disciples huddle around the gunwales looking up, torn sail and a lantern on the mast. Painting reaches all edges, no lettering or signature.

Daniel in indigo fringed cloak stands lower left looking up at several burning wheeled thrones in a white radiance above a Babylonian city; every throne seat is empty flame, with no face, hair or robe for the Ancient of Days. The thrones read a little like wheelchairs, and small fires burn in the city; dark painted edges all round, no lettering.
Watercolor of David reclining in green grass beside a still pool, with sheep, a stone fold and a crook nearby. The wash fades to white unpainted paper along the left, bottom and right edges.
Jonah sits hunched in a dark ribbed cavern over still water with a misty glow at the back opening; no figure in the glow; painting reaches all edges.

David's sling (left) still holds a stone in its pouch while a second stone hangs in mid-air above Goliath's helmet, and Goliath already lies on his side on the ground, so the stone is not shown striking his forehead. Saul and Abner stand on the valley floor right beside the fallen giant, in front of an army, instead of watching from the hillside.

Icon-style gold ground: Moses with staff raising his hand and Aaron in an ephod and breastplate stand centre among tents and Israelite families, a pig in the middle right, goats and sheep at the edges. The divine presence is only a ringed disc of light and smoke at top centre, with no figure; the breastplate shows stone ovals but no legible glyphs, and the painting runs to all borders.

Peter splashes into the shallows clutching his cloak, the beloved disciple points from the boat while others haul a net of fish, and Jesus stands on the shore by a charcoal fire. The top edge, especially the top-right corner, shows cream unpainted paper with a visible wash boundary.

Abraham raises the knife over Isaac bound hand and foot on the wood of a stone altar; tent and wind-bent trees at right; Isaac is shown as a bearded adult rather than a youth; sky clear of any figure.

Two mud-brick cities burn with heavy smoke rising from the ground, fleeing people and donkeys on the road; nothing falls from the sky, so the rain of sulfur and fire from a cloud is missing, and no face or figure appears in the smoke. The distant city at right shows a dome and minaret skyline, an anachronistic Islamic-era city.

Only one seraph is shown, top centre: two wings veil the face, but its bare feet hang uncovered below the lower wings, contradicting the verse, and it holds tongs with a live coal from verse 6. Isaiah is at lower left, and the bright cloud above is empty of any figure; full watercolour edges, no lettering.

Jonah sits hunched with bowed head in a ribbed, wet fish-belly cavern, with a faint glow at the far end and no figure in it. Dark grey-green wash reaches all four borders; the corners are mid-grey, not paper white.

A raised gold icon frame borders all four sides. Goliath already lies fallen and bleeding (centre) while a just-released stone is still in flight beside David's sling (left-centre), mixing two moments; Saul and Abner on the left hill.

Daniel stands in the den with sleeping lions, face lifted; beside him at left is a translucent winged female angel figure with clasped hands, though the scene asks for an unseen angel shown only as radiance. Darius leans on a low stone ledge at floor level inside the den (right), with a lion lying at his feet, rather than leaning over the rim above.

Ink-and-watercolour: Abraham holds a knife high at upper centre with his other hand on Isaac, a young bearded man roped across a stone altar heaped with wood; scrubby Moriah ridges, a wind-bent tree and a small tent are at right, with no divine figure in the pale sky. Isaac's dangling legs and Abraham's forward leg overlap awkwardly at lower left but read plausibly; pale sky and scrub washes reach all four edges, no lettering.

Icon style with gold sky: the father runs with cloak flying and arms wide as the bowed son reaches his chest, with villagers watching at the wall at left. Painted to all edges; a white columned building at right is a minor anachronism.
Fire and sulfur streak from a dark cloud (top centre) onto two walled burning cities with gardens between, fleeing figures at right and a distant town; the cloud has no face or figure.

Paul in a grey cloak with blank scrolls in his belt stands on a stony hillside path, face lifted, olive trees and stone walls around, village, coast and boats below, a few travellers (one in a red cloak) on the path. He fills the right foreground rather than being small, but the content matches; pale washes reach all edges and nothing is written on the scrolls.

Icon style: Saul, with a gold halo, walks centre with a staff and looks up into rays of light falling from the top edge, with no figure inside the light; two companions at left and two at right shield their eyes, and walled Damascus is at upper right. Gold ground and landscape reach all borders, no lettering.

Moses stretches his staff over a sea that is just dividing, under a cloud-and-fire column with no figure in it. Yet the right-hand water already holds submerged chariot wheels among the fish, a later moment (the Egyptians drowned) mixed into the dividing scene.
Wide renewed green land with river channels and no sea under a bright cloud-filled sky; no figure or face in the clouds; full-bleed.

Ezekiel stands at left, arm raised over a wide valley strewn with skulls, ribs and long bones under an amber sky, holding a blank wax tablet and stylus; no figure or face in the sky, so God is absent. Cream watercolour washes reach all four borders with no white band, and there is no lettering.

Icon-style gold-leaf border bands run down the left and right sides, outside the water walls, and a small red signature-like glyph sits in the lower-right corner (about x1260, y735). Otherwise the scene matches: families walk between the water walls, Moses is at right with his staff, and a cloud-and-fire pillar at top centre shows no face or figure.

The father runs with his hands on the bowed son's shoulders while villagers watch from the wall, but cream and white unpainted paper shows along the top edge and the left/bottom-left edge. A cursive, signature-like ink scrawl sits in the bottom-right corner (~x1250-1330, y740-760).
Icon-style gold sky with swirling pink and blue clouds over a dry open valley; no face or figure in the clouds; painting reaches all edges.

Exiles sit weeping on a reedy riverbank in the foreground, many with hands over their faces, with Babylon's walls, ziggurats and lit towers across the water at dusk. Painting reaches all edges; no lettering or signature.

Oil painting: white-bearded Moses with staff leads families carrying children along wet sand between towering green water walls; the only divine sign is a fiery glow inside dark clouds at top centre, with no figure. A small walled town sits on the far hill at right; dark painted edges all round, no lettering.

Light rays burst from the top centre over gold leaf, with dark swirling cloud, a dark sea and emerging rocks; there is no figure in the light. A thin dark-maroon painted border, about 6px, runs around all four edges.

The reclining shepherd with a gold halo, centre-parted long hair and beard (centre-right) reads strongly as a Christ icon rather than David, despite the lyre; a sword lies in the grass where the shepherd's crook was requested.

Peter runs across the shallows toward the lower left, away from the glowing Jesus on the far-right shore, and the beloved disciple in the boat also points left, away from Jesus; the charcoal fire burns inside the boat instead of on shore. The very pale washes fade into white paper along the left edge and the bottom-left and bottom-right corners.

Peter leaps from the boat into the shallows clutching his cloak, the young beloved disciple points toward the shore, and three disciples haul a net of fish at left; a small Jesus stands on the shore at right. The charcoal fire is a brazier inside the boat rather than on shore (a minor detail); paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

A column of pale light descends from the top centre through dark swirling mist onto dark waters, with rocks emerging at right. The zoomed light column shows no face or figure, and the paint reaches all four borders.
The Shulammite stands at left third gesturing toward roses and lilies, with vineyards and stone village at right and a shepherd's staff resting at lower left; no beloved figure shown.

A plain gold-leaf icon border runs down the left and right edges and across the top (only the bottom bleeds). God appears only as a pillar of cloud and fire at top centre with no form, and Moses (white beard, staff) leads the column between curling wave-walls; the gold sky is not the requested night turning to dawn.

Watercolour interior: the Levite stands centre with a knife held low and a staff, over the concubine lying on a mat; a donkey is in the doorway at left and a clay lamp on the bench at right. Her eyes look open, so she may read as alive, but the depiction is restrained; full edges, no lettering.

Four crouching Roman soldiers sort garments and hold dice, with the crucified Jesus at a distance and Jerusalem's walls at right. White unpainted paper shows on all four edges; the titulus has only faint smudges with no letterforms.
A painted red band about 9 px wide runs down both the left and right borders, and the foreground scroll on the wall is covered in legible-looking pseudo-Latin lettering.

Four kneeling legionaries in the centre hold up and sort garments while one lets lots fall from his hand, with a restrained distant crucifix at upper left (blank titulus, no lettering) and city walls at right. The painting bleeds on all four edges and there is no text on the shield or plaque.

Only one seraph is shown, top centre: a nearly nude, muscular bronze male figure with only a faint loincloth, its face visible under the upper wings and its bare feet uncovered, contrary to the verse; it holds tongs with a live coal from verse 6. Isaiah is at lower left with eyes downcast, and the bright cloud filling the sanctuary holds no divine figure; full oil-painted edges, no lettering.

Moses points toward the hills where a pig roots, Aaron stands beside him in an ornate jeweled breastplate rather than plain linen, and the crowd, tents and tabernacle smoke column appear with no figure in the smoke. The watercolor leaves white paper along all four edges.
Moses (left foreground) holds his staff out over the divided sea; the pillar of cloud and fire (centre-top) is swirling flame and vapour with no face; Egyptian chariots are tiny on the far shore.

Jesus' halo (centre-top) carries Greek-style glyphs (O / ω / N), and a flat gold icon border band runs down both the left and right edges. Otherwise the scene matches: wrapped Lazarus stands in the tomb doorway, Martha has hands to her chest, and crowds fill both lower corners.

Oil painting: David in a blue robe reclines on green grass in the lower-left foreground beside a still pool, with grazing sheep, a stone fold and terraced hills at right. He is larger in the frame than requested, and a lyre and sword lie in the grass at lower left instead of a crook (minor); paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

Icon-style village road with women (one carrying a water jar), two Roman soldiers and a child in a doorway, painted to all edges. The foreground scroll (~x430-910, y560-720) carries about 13 lines of dense pseudo-Greek capitals.

Child at centre with a cord among wolf and lamb, leopard and goat, calf and young lion; villagers watch at right and Jerusalem is faint on the hill; watercolor washes lighten slightly at the sides but drawing runs off every edge.

A child stands at centre with a raised hand, wolf and lambs and a leopard with a goat at left and calves and a lion at right, a walled village at left, and three small villagers at upper right; the gold sky reaches every edge with no border. The child wears a plain gold halo, which reads as a saint but carries no lettering; the lion is a full-grown maned adult rather than a young lion.

The watercolour vignettes into unpainted cream paper along the bottom edge, the lower-left corner and the right edge, and small white gaps break the sky wash along the top edge at upper left and right. The content matches: Paul, holding a scroll, pauses on a stony path looking up, above a coastal town and bay with boats, travellers and a Roman soldier on the road at lower right.

Fire streaks from a black cloud onto two burning walled cities on a green, palm-dotted plain, with fleeing figures on the road at right and sunrise at right; the clouds contain no face. White unpainted paper shows at the left, right and bottom-left edges.

Wall collapses as priests blow shofars (right) and Joshua and the people surge forward, but two separate gold Arks of the Covenant with cherubim appear in the crowd (far left and left-centre), duplicating a unique object.

Bald Elisha in a fur-collared mantle fills the left foreground while a band of youths pours from the city gate at upper right, pointing and jeering, with villagers in doorways and an altar-and-pole shrine on the ridge; the edges are full and there is no text. However, Elisha walks downhill toward the viewer, away from the gate, rather than climbing up toward Bethel as the verse and composition ask.

Ink-and-watercolour: green rolling hills run to a pale ochre plain on the horizon with no sea, under a luminous, nearly bare cream sky with cloud banks at upper left and right; no face or figure appears in the clouds. Edges are borderline: the land and clouds reach all borders, but the pale cream sky meets the left and right borders at mid-height and tiny white paper slivers show at the top-left and top-right corners, so it may read as a vignette into paper; no lettering.

Icon-style circular stone pit: Darius leans over the rim, Daniel stands centre with face lifted, and four lions lie with closed mouths. The angel appears only as translucent mandorla arcs with a faint wing outline beside Daniel, with no face or body. The view is from above, outdoors, rather than a low vantage, which is minor.

Pen-and-wash vignette fading into white paper on all four sides. Content matches: Moses pointing, Aaron in high-priest vestments, pig rooting at right, and smoke/glow over the tabernacle with no figure.

In this watercolour, light bursts through dark mist from the upper centre over dark rippling waters, with a dark land-mass emerging at centre-left. Close inspection of the bright area shows no face or figure, and the wash reaches all four edges.

Two near-identical kings in purple and gold court robes lean over the pit rim at top centre where one Darius was requested, and a faint but clearly human robed angel with face and hands stands beside Daniel at centre-right, although the scene asked for only the radiance of an unseen angel. Daniel stands centre among four sleeping lions; grey washes reach every edge, no lettering.

Oil scene: Moses with staff raises his hand to the crowd of men, women and children; Aaron wears a breastplate and headband; tents surround the tabernacle, which has a pale smoke plume and no figure; a dark pig roots among goats at right. The top-left is hazy painted sky, not paper, so the edges are full.
Jonah sits hunched on dark water inside the ribbed fish interior with faint glowing pockets in the walls (no faces or figures); gold ground in the top corners is icon background, not a border.

Seven exiles in worn tunics sit among the reeds on both lower sides, several with faces in their hands, beside still water at dusk, with Babylon's walls, ziggurats and lamp-lit gate across the river at upper right. The painting is full-bleed on all edges, with no lettering on the gates or walls.

Ink-and-watercolour: green rolling hills and wildflowers fill the lower half with no sea, under blue and violet cloud banks parting around a bright pale centre; no face or figure appears in the clouds or the light. White paper shows only as sky light between clouds, and washes reach all four borders; no lettering.

Oil scene: the father, cloak flying, runs in and embraces the bowed, ragged son's head on a dusty road, with villagers at the wall at left, terraced hills and a lake beyond. Painted to all four borders.
Goliath already lies face-down (centre) while David's sling pouch (upper left) still holds an unreleased stone, contradicting the moment; Saul and Abner watch from the upper right.

The open scroll on the wall in the lower-centre foreground is covered in dense pseudo-script glyph lines (the scene asked for written lines, but they read as gibberish lettering). Villagers, a woman with a water jar at right, a child in the left doorway and Roman soldiers in the distance match the request, and the watercolour reaches all four edges.

Icon style: Joshua, with sword and spear, strides over the collapsing wall at centre amid billowing dust at lower left; white-capped priests blow ram's horns behind him, others carry the ark at right, the crowd surges in from the right, and townsfolk watch from inside Jericho. Gold ground reaches all borders, and the marks at the lower right are grass tufts, not lettering.

Icon style: Peter steps from the boat onto the waves toward Jesus, who stands on the water at right, with disciples in the boat and light breaking through dark cloud. A pale cursive signature-like scrawl sits in the bottom-right corner (~x1265-1330, y700-725); the gold sky rather than night is a minor point.
Foreground scroll on the wall (centre-bottom) is filled with dense lines of pseudo-script; villagers, two Roman soldiers, a woman with a jar and a child at a doorway match the scene.

Elderly Adam lies at centre-right on a woven mat with eyes closed and hands folded, a plain gold halo with no lettering behind his head, and six kin kneeling or prostrate around him at left. Tents, a mud-brick house, a well with jars and tools, and grazing goats fill the right, and the gold sky and hills reach all four edges.

A huge embroidered blue-and-gold robe train with no wearer spills across the floor and over two altars on both sides of the lower frame, a literal rendering of God's robe ('his train filled the temple'), so it counts as clothing for God. One seraph at top centre in a white robe holds tongs with a coal, and one wing only partly veils its golden face; Isaiah looks up in the foreground, the gold ground and floor reach all borders, and there is no lettering.

Radiant rays pour from the top centre over gold, with dark swirling cloud, a deep blue sea and a rocky island emerging. The zoomed light source shows no figure, and the paint reaches all four edges with no border.

Bald Elisha with staff walks toward the viewer, away from the gate (left), while youths stream out of the Bethel gate pointing and jeering (right), with a golden calf atop the city; he is not shown climbing toward the gate.

Paul walks a stony hillside path with his face slightly lifted, above a walled village and a harbour with boats, with olive trees, travellers and two red-cloaked soldiers at lower right; the painting is full-bleed and the scroll in his belt is blank. He is large and central rather than the small lower-middle figure the composition requested.

A faint pale cursive signature-like scrawl is painted into the ground in the lower-right corner (about x1260-1330, y730-750). The scene otherwise matches: Joshua with a spear leads a shouting crowd forward at centre, white-turbaned priests blow ram's horns and carry the ark at right, the wall collapses in dust behind them, and paint reaches all edges.

Jericho's wall collapses in dust while the crowd shouts, Joshua points with a spear at centre, and priests carry the ark blowing shofars at right. The watercolor wash stops short of white deckled paper at the top-left, top-right, right and bottom-right corners.
A white-bearded old man in robes with a radiant head sits on the central throne, depicting God in human form; a small group of unrequested people also stands in a doorway at left.

Semi-transparent, ghostly washed-out traveller figures stand inside the light beams just left of Saul (about x 480–530) and in a cluster just right of him (about x 790–860), which reads as apparitions within the light that the scene excluded. Otherwise Saul shades his eyes under a blank shaft of light, companions recoil on both sides, and Damascus sits at upper right.

The watercolour washes stop short of the paper edge: the blue sky wash ends in a ragged line with white paper beyond it at the top-left and top-right corners, and the left and lower edges fade into unpainted cream paper. The content matches: Abraham raises a knife at upper centre over a bearded young Isaac roped on wood atop a stone altar, with a tent at right, a rising sun at upper right and no divine figure.

Peter leaps from the boat clutching his cloak toward the haloed Jesus on the shore by the fire. A second Jesus-like figure with a halo, in a red robe, stands in the boat pointing (~x430-640, y130-530), so Jesus appears twice and no distinct beloved disciple is shown.
Jesus stands before the open tomb with arm extended calling, Martha beside him with hand to chest, and Lazarus in white linen emerges at the dark entrance (right); crowd frames the foreground.

The scroll on the elder's knees (lower centre-right) is filled with dense pseudo-script glyph lines that his finger points to. Otherwise it matches: a young listener stands in the doorway, there is a lit lamp on the ledge and a jar at left, and the watercolour reaches all edges, though the sky at upper left is very pale.

Jesus's cross nimbus at centre-left carries Greek letters (O, O, N, for 'O ON') in its arms, which is visible lettering. The scene otherwise matches: Jesus gestures toward Lazarus, who stands wrapped in grave linens in the dark tomb mouth, haloed Martha has hands at her chest at left, and the crowd fills both sides; the gold ground reaches all borders.

Four winged, eye-covered creatures (lion, ox, man-faced, eagle) flank an empty, radiant jeweled throne under a rainbow above a crystal sea; the throne holds no figure. The man-faced creature is icon-like but belongs to the formed creatures; Byzantine domed churches with crosses behind are a minor anachronism.
The Shulammite stands at left third among roses and lilies gesturing toward the valley, with a staff, vineyards and village beyond; full-bleed.

The open scroll on the stone wall across the lower foreground is covered in columns of dense pseudo-script glyphs. Otherwise the street scene matches: two Roman soldiers walk the road at centre, a woman with a jar and a child in the doorway are at right, and villagers are at left, with the oil painting full-bleed on all edges.

Ink-and-watercolour: Daniel in an indigo cloak with blue fringe stands on rocks at left gazing at several empty burning thrones with fiery spoked wheels, set on a radiant platform amid storm clouds above a Babylonian city with ziggurats. No face, hair or robe appears on any throne; washes reach all borders apart from a tiny white sliver at the bottom-right corner, and there is no lettering.

The sling flies off top-left with a stone still in its pouch (~x110-220, y135-220) while a stone strikes Goliath's forehead (~x1130, y385), a contradictory object state. Goliath falls backward face-up rather than on his face, and white paper borders all four edges.

Icon-style Abraham raises the knife over Isaac lying on the wood of the altar, with the tent and wind-bent trees present; a second knife rests on the altar stones as the scene requested; gold sky contains no figure.

A seated, draped white-robed form with lap and knees fills the jewelled throne at centre, its head lost in a burst of light, so God appears with a robed body. An unselected red-robed standing figure (elder-like) stands beside the throne at right-centre. The four winged creatures (man, lion, calf, eagle-headed robed figure) stand on a shard-strewn glassy sea, and the painting is full-bleed.

Oil painting: white-bearded Moses in a cloak stands in the left foreground, arm stretched out with a crook staff, as a dry sandy path opens between churning waves into the distance, under a fire-lit column of cloud at top centre that shows no face or figure. Odd wheel ruts mark the seabed path, and a walled town and road sit on the right shore; paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

Bald Elisha in a fur mantle walks toward the viewer down the path away from Bethel's gate, rather than uphill toward it, while about 11 youths pour from the gate pointing and jeering. Women watch from doorways and a golden-calf shrine stands on the ridge top-right; painted to all edges.
Ezekiel raises one arm over the bone-strewn valley but holds a modern clipboard with a metal clip and a pencil in his other hand (centre-right), an obvious anachronism.

David at left still has a stone loaded in his raised sling pouch while a second stone flies past Goliath's shoulder at right as he topples sideways, so the moment is contradictory, and the stone is not in his forehead nor is he falling face-first. Watercolour washes fade to white paper at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners; Saul and Abner watch from the hill and the Philistines are at right.

Oil painting: Peter strides barefoot over dark churning waves in the centre foreground toward Jesus, who stands upright on the water at right, while about eight disciples with oars watch from the boat at left; moonlight breaks through clouds at top. Peter oddly carries a staff and a fishing net (a minor detail); paint reaches all edges, no lettering.

Elderly Adam lies on a woven mat with eyes closed and hands folded, family members kneel around him, and there are tents, a well, a mudbrick house, goats, a jar and tools. The watercolor leaves white unpainted paper along the left and right edges and all four corners.
Jesus stands in the boat with arm outstretched over the water as huddled disciples cling to the gunwales; lantern on the mast, torn sail and shore town match the scene.
